title: Americans Want Cars That Work Like Smartphones
paragraphs: Smartphones have changed the way people shop, pay and find information. Now, according to a new survey, many Americans want their cars to work in a similar way.

The survey was commissioned by Verra Mobility, a US company that provides technology for transportation, such as toll and parking payment systems. In May 2026, it asked 2,000 American adults who owned or leased a car made in 2019 or later about connected vehicle services. These are services that use a car's built-in communication technology, rather than connecting to a smartphone through systems like Apple CarPlay or Android Auto.

The survey found that 72% of people expect their next car to work like a smartphone, with built-in apps and services. In addition, 51% said that connected features would influence their decision to buy a different car model or a more expensive version. The number of people using these services is also growing. Around 54% said they use at least one connected service provided by their car's manufacturer, up from 49% in 2024.

People are especially interested in features that make driving easier. Around 72% said they would like their car to suggest places for parking, fuel or electric vehicle charging, and help with tolls. Also, 66% liked the idea of not having to connect their smartphone every time they drive, and 51% said they would be comfortable with their car paying for tolls and parking automatically.
Younger people were especially interested. For example, 67% of people aged 18 to 24 use a connected service, compared with 44% of people aged 55 to 64.

However, many people are unsure about privacy. Only 14% said they fully understand what data their car collects, down from 22% in 2024. In addition, 54% had at least some concerns about how their data is collected. Even so, 66% said they would share their driving and location data in exchange for benefits such as insurance discounts.
According to Cathi Chinn, a vice president at Verra Mobility, consumers have now fully arrived in the connected vehicle category.
